topic: Candlestick pattern vocabulary census (TA-Lib 61 patterns on MNQ)
purpose: Counts how many candlestick patterns exist and fire in MNQ (TA-Lib 0.7.1, 5 timeframes, 2021-2025) and how many are measurable; cuts by candle length; compares 7 pattern registries on the machine. Reads lake table derived/mnq_candlestick_pattern_census/recipe=candlestick_pattern_census_v1 (305 rows = 61 patterns x 5 timeframes).
findings: 61 TA-Lib candlestick patterns; 59 fire at least once; kicking and kickingbylength never fire (SQL on census table: fires_any=59; zero-sum patterns = kicking, kickingbylength).
2,275,881 bar readings scanned (1m 1,767,369 + 5m 353,478 + 15m 117,826 + 1h 29,497 + 4h 7,711; SQL sum bar_count_scanned/pattern) and 4,378,198 total firings (SQL sum firing_count_total).
Patterns measurable (>=60 holdout-2025 firings): 50 at 1m, 37 at 5m, 32 at 15m, 23 at 1h, 13 at 4h (SQL count of meets_minimum_firing_count_on_holdout per timeframe).
Split by candle length: 13 single-candle, 19 two, 21 three, 4 four, 4 five (SQL distinct pattern by candle_count).
Mean CNN recognition AUC across the table = 0.9887 (SQL avg recognition_area_under_curve).

Notebook prose states 883 scorecard tests, 72 distinct (pattern,side) pairs, 0 survivors after Benjamini-Yekutieli; the 883 and 0 reproduce from the scorecard table (SQL: n=883, surv=0); the 72 is hardcoded text I did not re-derive.

lookahead_detail: Pure counts of pattern firings; no forward returns. The registry table (cell near line 637) is hardcoded definition counts, not computed.
edge_summary: No edge claimed or tested here; it is a vocabulary/coverage census. Its only trading-relevant statement (883 tests, 0 survivors) is inherited from the scorecard.
methods: Aggregations of a landed census table with marimo controls (min-firing slider, timeframe, candle-count filter), eight-number stats, histograms.
data_sources: s3://derived/mnq_candlestick_pattern_census/recipe=candlestick_pattern_census_v1 (MNQ, 1m/5m/15m/1h/4h, 2021-2025, holdout = 2025); built by datalake/scripts/build_candlestick_pattern_census.py
validity_issues: Hardcoded numbers in prose (61, 72, 883, 0, '13 single-candle', registry counts) are not computed from the table, so they can drift.
The 'only 13 of 61 are single candle' claim is definitional (TA-Lib lookback), not a market finding.
Firing counts pool 5 timeframes of the same underlying minutes, so they are not independent.
recommendation: Use as the reference for which TA-Lib columns are worth carrying: drop kicking and kickingbylength, treat each pattern side as one hypothesis, and restrict any pattern-derived input to the 50 patterns with >=60 holdout firings at 1m. Do not treat pattern presence as a profit source for the 40% / 2:1 target.

topic: Do candlestick patterns predict direction after costs (MNQ 2025 holdout)
purpose: Scores every TA-Lib pattern side x timeframe x forward horizon on the 2025 holdout: forward close-to-close move when fired vs not fired, bootstrap interval on the difference, dollars per contract vs round-trip cost, Benjamini-Yekutieli correction; contrasts with the CNN's near-perfect pattern recognition.
findings: 883 pattern-side-timeframe-horizon tests, 50 patterns, 5 timeframes; 0 survive Benjamini-Yekutieli at q=0.10 (SQL: n=883, surv=0, minimum bootstrap p = 0.00025).

55 tests have a bootstrap interval excluding zero and 13 do so AND exceed the $2.80 round-trip cost, uncorrected; chance supplies ~44.2 false positives at 5% (SQL: sigzero=55, nominal=13; false_positives_expected=44.15).

The 13 'nominal' winners are tiny-sample cells: e.g. 4h hikkake bullish k=6 n=64 +$236.69 p=0.0003; 4h hikkake k=3 n=83 +$108.16; 15m dojistar bearish n~130 +$18 to +$34; 1h belthold bullish n=343 +$28.75 p=0.044 (SQL listing of interval_excludes_zero AND covers_round_trip_cost).
Round-trip cost = $2.8011 per MNQ contract (5.6022 ticks) from cost_model.json; edge dollars = difference in average ranges x average_range_points x $2 per point (notebook lines 216-221).

Mean CNN recognition AUC 0.9887 over 54 patterns; hammer 0.966, engulfing 0.995 (notebook prose line 77 and census SQL avg 0.9887); recognition AUC vs earned dollars correlation is reported by the notebook as ~0 (panel C computed live; not re-run by me).

Notebook cites the independent build_findings_casebook.py screen: 1,138 tests, one discovery survivor (1m bullish engulfing, long, next candle), failed 2024 validation at t=1.581, one-sided p=0.0569, day-shifted placebo 0 survivors in 20 of 20 (prose lines 543-546; the engulfing/2024 numbers are confirmed in the candle-vectors frozen_rules table: validation t=1.581, p=0.0569).
lookahead_detail: Forward move is measured from the signal candle's CLOSE to the close of candle k (build_candle_pattern_scorecard.py lines 26-30, 220), i.e. it includes the close-to-next-open jump that no order can capture (2.0 ticks mean per what_to_encode Panel D). Entry at a price that has already printed slightly overstates edge, but every result is null anyway. Recognition AUC comes from a CNN trained on synthetic data, so no leakage. Holdout split is a fixed date split (2025).
edge_summary: No pattern trades profitably after costs on the 2025 holdout once the number of tests is corrected: 0 of 883 survive Benjamini-Yekutieli, and the 13 uncorrected cost-clearing cells (5 timeframe/side combinations with n<150 dominate) are below the ~44 false positives chance supplies. Up-rate when fired sits near the baseline (~0.5). Recognition is solved (AUC 0.989) but direction is not; correlation between the two is ~0.
validity_issues: 883 correlated tests on one 2025 year; a single year cannot support a rule.
Several 'significant' cells have n=64-140 firings (4h hikkake n=64/83, 15m dojistar n~130).
Entry at signal-bar close (untradeable jump included) rather than next open.
Bootstrap p-values resolution 0.00025 (4000 resamples).
Scorecard covers only holdout 2025; no discovery/validation split for the same tests.
recommendation: Do not give the model a candlestick-direction objective or rely on TA-Lib pattern flags as alpha. Keep recognition-grade pattern flags only as cheap context features. Close this line of research as the notebook itself concludes.

topic: Learning TA-Lib's 13 single-candle rules from geometry vs geometry+context
purpose: Fits four model families (logistic regression, depth-4 tree, gradient-boosted trees, MLP) to recover each of 13 single-candle TA-Lib labels from (a) the candle's shape only and (b) shape plus 10-bar trailing averages; shows the rule depends on 10 bars of context.
findings: Best from shape only vs shape+10-bar context, averaged over 13 patterns: gradient boosting balanced accuracy 0.842 vs 0.993, MLP 0.836 vs 0.985, depth-4 tree 0.827 vs 0.919, logistic 0.777 vs 0.841 (SQL on derived/mnq_single_candle_recognizer_study).
GBT with context: AUC 0.99995, average precision 0.9991; without context AUC 0.971 (same SQL).
Split is time-ordered 70/30 with a 10-bar purge (build_single_candle_recognizer_study.py lines 89, 309-312).
Recognises a deterministic rule (labels are functions of the inputs), so high scores mean the model recovered arithmetic, not market structure.
Training seconds per pattern: GBT 5.5 s, MLP 4.4 s, logistic 0.34 s.
lookahead_detail: Labels are TA-Lib outputs computed from the same bars; trailing averages use the 10 previous bars only. No forward returns.
edge_summary: No trading edge tested. It shows a tree/GBT can reproduce hand rules almost perfectly once trailing context is supplied, which means a downstream model that receives trailing range/body context does not need TA-Lib pattern flags at all.
methods: Binary classifiers per pattern; balanced accuracy, AP, AUC, F1; interactive TA-Lib arithmetic explorer for thresholds.
data_sources: s3://derived/mnq_single_candle_recognizer_study/recipe=single_candle_recognizer_v1 (104 rows = 4 models x 2 feature sets x 13 patterns); underlying MNQ bars, single timeframe (see build script), time-ordered split
validity_issues: Task is reproducing a deterministic rule; scores do not transfer to any market question.
Single 70/30 time split, no repeated folds.
Model choice takeaway ('use GBT') is about rule recovery only.
recommendation: Nothing to train from here. Useful only as a guarantee that giving the multimodal model 10-bar trailing range and body context is sufficient to subsume the single-candle TA-Lib flags, so those flags can be dropped rather than encoded.

topic: Does a frozen pretrained candle-pattern CNN embedding predict direction?
purpose: Tests transfer of the chart_cnn checkpoint (cnn_patterns.pt, 256-d embedding trained on 12.3M synthetic candle images to recognise 61 TA-Lib patterns) as an encoder for direction on real MNQ 5m windows, fitted on 2024, scored once on 2025, against an information-free shuffled-embedding control and a label-permutation null.
findings: Model saw only 5 candles (windows: 37,264 of 1 candle, 20,717 of 2, 21,050 of 3, 6,266 of 4, 5,769 of 5; notebook line 106).
61 labels explain only ~25% of the embedding: mean R^2 0.247, median 0.221, range 0.041 to 0.829 over 256 coordinates (SQL on derived/mnq_frozen_encoder_probe).

Direction AUC on 2025 (test_row_count ~39-40k): 1 candle ahead embedding_256 0.4977 vs shuffled control 0.4967 (null95 0.5037); 2 ahead 0.4990 vs shuffled 0.5057 (shuffled 'beats its null'); 6 ahead 0.5002 vs shuffled 0.4987. Encoder never clears its null (SQL).
candle_geometry_5 (5 raw numbers) gets 0.5051 / 0.5079 / 0.5056 at k=1/2/6; only k=2 clears its null (0.5079 > 0.5070) (SQL).
labels_61 0.4966-0.4974 and probabilities_61 0.4939-0.4991: below 0.5.

Cited independent results: direction CNN on rendered images 0.504 OOS vs 1-D numeric control 0.506; every candle-shape statistic |corr| < 0.005 with next return across 646,932 bars (analytics/docs/FINDINGS.md section 3); label-free encoders lose to raw controls (AE hammer AP 0.0433 vs raw 0.4981; 0 of 132 direction tests significant under BH, median AUC 0.5018) (prose lines 396-424).
lookahead_detail: Embeddings were computed from past 5-candle windows and joined to forward returns; fit 2024 / score 2025; includes permutation-null and shuffled-embedding control, which guards against spurious gains. The notebook itself retracts its earlier recommendation to freeze the encoder.
edge_summary: No directional information in the frozen encoder or in any sibling feature block: AUCs 0.494-0.508 on ~40k 2025 rows, with the information-free shuffled control scoring as high (0.5057) as the encoder (0.4990). Directional edge of raw geometry is at best 0.0079 AUC.
methods: Ridge from 61 labels to 256 embedding coordinates (R^2); logistic-style direction probes on five feature blocks with 2024 fit / 2025 test, shuffled control, label-permutation null.
data_sources: s3://derived/mnq_frozen_encoder_probe/recipe=frozen_candle_encoder_probe_v1 (Ridge R^2 rows + direction rows for k=1,2,6); s3://derived/mnq_next_candles_5m (MNQ 5m holdout bars); MNQ 5m, fit 2024, test 2025
validity_issues: Only AUC, no cost or PnL; horizons 1, 2, 6 only.
Only three horizons and one timeframe (5m).
Linear-style probes; a nonlinear head was not tested on the embedding.
Prose contains a self-correction, so read the verdict block, not the intro.
recommendation: Do not use the chart_cnn embedding or the 61-label/probability vectors as direction features. If a candle representation is wanted, use raw normalised candle parts (body, shadows, close position, gap in average ranges); nothing learned has beaten them. The soft pattern probability may be kept only as a data-quality margin instrument.

topic: Incremental feature ladder on MNQ 5m: which blocks earn their place, per target
purpose: Adds six causal feature blocks one at a time (range memory, momentum level, volatility rate of change, momentum rate of change, volume level, volume-conditioned body) and scores each rung on 2025 (fit 2021-2023) against best-of-five shuffled-block controls, for four targets: next-bar direction, range, signed open gap, gap magnitude. Also relates the close-to-next-open gap to the bid-ask spread.
findings: Test rows ~69,871 (5m, 2025 holdout, 353,478 bars total; SQL on derived/mnq_feature_ladder).

Direction (AUC): intercept 0.500, range memory 0.5010, momentum level 0.5046, vol rate-of-change 0.5075, momentum ROC 0.5092, volume level 0.5098, volume-conditioned body 0.5088. Ladder max 0.5098; the notebook says every gain is inside shuffle noise but the table flags momentum_level, volume_level and volume_conditioned_body as beating the best-of-five shuffle (SQL), so the prose overstates 'dead' while the effect size (~0.01 AUC) is not tradeable.
Next-bar range R^2: 0.0387 (range memory), 0.0440, 0.0569, 0.0566, 0.0828 (volume level +0.0261), 0.0869 final; volatility rate-of-change +0.0129, momentum ROC -0.0003 (SQL).
Signed open gap R^2 stays negative (-0.0037 to -0.0025): unforecastable (SQL).
Gap magnitude R^2 rises from -0.0305 to 0.1174; volume level +0.0388 and volume_conditioned_body +0.0946 (best-of-five shuffle +0.0243) (SQL).

Mean close-to-next-open gap 0.5009 points = 2.00 ticks vs measured quoted spread 0.5105 points (ratio 0.981) from 1,348,266 quotes; bars at session edges 0.38% of holdout (prose lines 254-268; hardcoded, not recomputed by me).
Prose states range-memory volume-first vs derivatives-first order test: vol ROC +0.0129 vs +0.0156, volume_conditioned_body +0.0946 vs +0.0948 (order-robust) (prose lines 450-455).
lookahead_detail: Features are trailing and shifted (build_feature_ladder.py lines 134-198, e.g. bar_range.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=window)); every feature is shifted at least one bar, so 'this candle' columns (body_per_unit_volume_this_candle) actually describe the PREVIOUS bar (lines 192-193) - misnamed, conservative rather than leaky. Targets are divided by average_range_10_bars computed on prior bars. Fit/score by sample_split (discovery vs holdout).
edge_summary: Direction is not forecastable (AUC <= 0.5098, ~0.01 above coin flip, unexpressed in dollars). What is forecastable is the size of the next bar: R^2 0.0869 for next-bar range and 0.117 for close-to-next-open gap magnitude, driven by volume level and body-per-volume (a price-impact / execution-cost proxy). This supports volatility and slippage sizing, not a 40% win / 2:1 payoff.
methods: Feature ladder with GBT-style scorers, best-of-five shuffled control, AUC for direction and R^2 for magnitudes; spread comparison against quoted ticks.
data_sources: s3://derived/mnq_feature_ladder/recipe=feature_ladder_v1 (28 rows: 7 rungs x 4 targets); s3://derived/mnq_feature_ladder_volume_first; s3://derived/mnq_next_candles_5m/recipe=pattern_forward_candles_v1; MNQ 5m, fit 2021-2023, score 2025
validity_issues: R^2 targets are normalised by 10-bar average range so levels are not comparable to analytics/volrange (0.6677).
Single 5m timeframe and a single holdout year.
Direction flags contradict prose: three rungs flagged as beating shuffle.
Spread claim rests on a 1.35M-quote sample that is hardcoded text.
recommendation: Take volatility/range and execution-cost forecasts (range memory, volume level, vol rate of change, body per unit volume) as inputs for stop/target sizing and slippage estimation; do not expect them to supply direction. Add order-flow from tick data (Databento mbp-1 not yet promoted) if direction is to be attempted.

topic: Volume encodings vs candle body/wick anatomy (contemporaneous, MNQ 2021-2025)
purpose: Measures which encoding of volume (raw, bar height in trailing window, trailing z-score, trailing rank, colour-signed) relates to which part of the same candle (upper wick, lower wick, body, ratios), with Spearman, mutual information vs Gaussian equivalent, decile medians, colour split and a bid-ask-bounce control.
findings: 8,800 rows across 5 timeframes (SQL count on derived/mnq_volume_candle_anatomy).
Mean |Spearman| by volume encoding (non-tautological pairings, bars closing inside range): rank 0.2101, z-score 0.2050, bar height 0.1941, raw contracts 0.1724, colour-signed 0.0375 (SQL).
Best |Spearman| by candle part: total range 0.826, absolute body 0.503, lower wick 0.495, upper wick 0.408, body fraction 0.150, wick asymmetry 0.060, signed body 0.016 (SQL).

5m, volume_rank_trailing: range Spearman 0.375 (MI 0.164 nats), absolute body 0.249 (0.068), signed body -0.0055 (MI 0.0616 nats) with 342,661 bars (SQL): information exists but is direction-blind (heteroscedastic).
Notebook prose: volume vs range Pearson +0.803 on 647,416 1m candles, 11.0x range spread across volume deciles (cited from analytics/volrange, not recomputed).
All trailing statistics are shifted one bar with min_periods equal to the window (build_volume_candle_anatomy.py lines 125-135, 173).
lookahead_detail: The relationships are CONTEMPORANEOUS: the current bar's volume is correlated with the same bar's range/wick, so it is descriptive and would leak if used to predict that bar's own shape. Trailing z-score/rank denominators are lagged one bar (lines 133-135). No forward returns.
edge_summary: No predictive claim is made or tested. The strongest results are volume-range and volume-body-size linkages (|rho| up to 0.83), i.e. volatility/activity structure; volume has essentially no linear relation to signed body (-0.0055).
methods: Spearman/Pearson, kNN mutual information (k=3), conditional medians per volume decile, rising vs falling split, close-inside-range bounce control.
data_sources: s3://derived/mnq_volume_candle_anatomy/recipe=volume_candle_anatomy_v1 (MNQ 1m,5m,15m,1h,4h, 2021-2025); s3://derived/mnq_next_candles_5m for the interactive window
validity_issues: Contemporaneous correlations, no train/test split.
Panel G recommends interaction features and a family-classifier reorder but no model was fitted to confirm gain.
MI estimate of 0.06 nats with rho~0 is a heteroscedasticity effect and carries no directional signal.
recommendation: Use trailing volume rank/z-score (lagged) as a volatility/size-of-move covariate for the multimodal model's risk and stop-sizing head, not as a direction feature. Prefer volume_rank_trailing over raw volume; gate any new column with the bounce control.
reusable_assets: Feature names: volume_rank_trailing_120_bars, volume_zscore_trailing_120_bars, wick_asymmetry_upper_minus_lower (listed in notebook panel G)

topic: Fat tails as a sampling artifact: time bars vs volume/dollar bars
purpose: Shows fat-tailed returns are partly an artifact of clock-time sampling by re-sampling 1m futures bars on volume or dollar clocks with the same bar count and comparing excess kurtosis and sigma exceedances; interactive by root, bar size, threshold.
findings: Notebook cannot open as written: it opens E:/lake/_meta/tails.duckdb (line 37) but that path does not exist; scripts/tails_app.py builds E:/lake-workspace/tails.duckdb (1.3 MB, present).
No numbers are stored in the file; prose lines 254-255 hardcode '45 monsters in 6,399 bars' and '0.4 extreme bars' for a bell curve, from a past run I could not re-run.

My own check on calendar bars: MNQ 4h bars 2021-2025 (7,994 returns, raw not back-adjusted) excess kurtosis 14.67, skew 0.15, 47 bars beyond 4 sigma versus ~1.0 expected under a normal (dashboard SQL on ohlcv_4h).
Volume/dollar clocks are built by accumulating 1m bars until cumulative volume crosses total_volume/target_bars (src/lake/clocks.py lines 43-69, 96).
lookahead_detail: clocks.resample calibrates the threshold as total/target_bars where total is the whole-series volume, so bar boundaries depend on future volume (clocks.py line 96); standardise() uses whole dev-span mean/std (tailviz.py standardise); futures come from fmadj back-adjusted series whose adjustment uses later rolls. Acceptable for a distribution study, not for a live sampler. A bar closes on the crossing 1m bar (not early), which is causal.
edge_summary: No edge tested; a descriptive study of return distribution shape under different sampling clocks. The practical value is for label/sizing design (barriers in sigma units, sizing off fat tails).
methods: Excess kurtosis, skew, exceedance counts vs 68-95-99.7, per-hour and per-year breakdown of extreme bars, matched bar counts across clocks.
data_sources: E:/lake-workspace/tails.duckdb (intended) built from bars/fmadj macros; futures roots, 1m base, dev span = first 80% of history (final fifth sealed)
validity_issues: Broken database path.
Stats reproduce only after the app rebuilds the workspace DB.
Hardcoded prose numbers.
Whole-series threshold calibration.
recommendation: Adopt as design guidance, not a dataset: label barriers and position sizing must assume fat tails (kurtosis ~15 on 4h bars) and consider dollar/volume bars for label sampling only if the threshold is rolling and causal. Do not copy clocks.resample into a live pipeline without making the threshold trailing.

topic: Candle windows as vectors: recogniser, nearest-neighbour forecasts, learned shape codes, pre-registered next-candles screen
purpose: Builds 16-bar OHLC windows normalised to average range (64-d shape vector) and an 11-d market-state vector; trains hammer/engulfing/harami/doji recognisers; uses an HNSW vector store for nearest-neighbour direction forecasts; learns label-free shape embeddings; and runs a frozen pre-registered screen (discovery 2021-2023 -> validate 2024 -> holdout 2025) of every pattern side and shape code over the next 1-6 candles with costs.
findings: Recogniser on 1m 2025 held out: neural network mean AP 0.983 (min 0.961), GBT 0.976, logistic 0.381; on unseen 1h: NN 0.930, GBT 0.860; 4h: NN 0.887 (AP, 7 patterns; embedded results DB).

Nearest-neighbour direction votes: 396 tests, median AUC 0.5012 (range 0.305-0.713), 0 with Benjamini-Hochberg q<0.10; e.g. 1m random 2025 bars k=50 shape AUC 0.4959-0.4975 vs null95 0.5053-0.5056 (embedded DB neighbour_forecast_evaluation).
Last-bar-reversal baseline scores AUC 0.514-0.517 at 1m one bar ahead, better than the neighbour votes (notebook lines 704-708; DB shows 0.5170 market / 0.5143 shape at 1m k=1).

Pre-registered screen: 569 pattern sides x each of two questions; 192 enter the screen per question; only 1 survives (unconditional 1m bullish engulfing, long, candle 1: discovery t=5.27, +0.0145 avg ranges); 0 survive question B (matched baseline); placebo 95th percentile 0 survivors over 20 sets (DB next_candles_screen/placebo).
That rule failed 2024 validation: t=1.581, one-sided p=0.0569 (23,356 firings), Holm p 0.0569, holdout never opened; tradeable_edge_in_holdout False (DB next_candles_frozen_rules).
Cost: 5.6022 ticks round trip (2.8011 dollars), 7.6022 under stress; entry at next open, exit at candle k close (DB next_candles_run_information).
Bar counts 2021-2025: 1m 1,767,369; 5m 353,478; 15m 117,826; 1h 29,497; 4h 7,711; typical 10-bar average range 4.75 / 11.25 / 19.5 / 41 / 91 ticks (median) (DB next_candles_bars).

Label-free shape encoders lose to raw controls: AE hammer AP 0.0433 vs raw 0.4981; masked-candle model coordinate correlates 0.5658 with ATR percentile (volatility, not shape) (notebook cell quoted in frozen_candle_encoder prose, and DB shape_embedding_* tables).

Pattern 'what follows' effect at 1m is a sliver against the textbook: next bar ~0.015 average ranges lower after a hammer, 0.01 lower after bullish engulfing (prose lines 616-620), too small to trade.
lookahead_detail: Section 10 is designed against leakage: entries at the next candle open, horizons stop at session gaps/contract changes, matched-baseline GBT cross-fitted by year on 2021-2023 then frozen for 2024-2025, placebo firings shifted whole trading days, 2025 unopened unless 2024 passes. Section 4/6 neighbour corpus built only from windows whose outcome closed before 2025 (notebook 7 lines 790-793). Standardisation uses 2021-2024 mean/sd. Residual issue: 0.2-0.9% of 1m hammer/harami/doji labels sit on the wrong side of boundary in the vector after dividing by R_t (line 376-379).
edge_summary: Across five timeframes, 569 pattern sides/shape codes, two baselines, day-clustered t-tests and placebos, exactly one candidate survived discovery (1m bullish engulfing, +0.0145 average ranges = about 0.07 ticks-equivalent), failed 2024 validation (p=0.057), and never reached holdout; nothing survives the matched-baseline test. Nearest-neighbour direction AUC is a coin flip (0.4959-0.5069 at 1m, 0 of 396 significant). Only volatility-like effects and a tiny 1m mean-reversion of the last bar (AUC 0.514-0.517) appear.
methods: 64-d ratio-normalised windows, HNSW nearest neighbours (DuckDB vss), neural/GBT/logistic recognisers, day-block bootstrap, permutation null, BH/BY/Holm corrections, autoencoder/VQ/masked models, cross-fitted HistGradientBoosting matched baseline, placebo shifts.

topic: TA-Lib indicators and candlestick patterns vs next-bar direction, MNQ
purpose: Score all TA-Lib indicators and 61 candlestick patterns as predictors of direction at h=1,4,12 bars on 1m/1h/4h MNQ bars, with block-bootstrap intervals, circular-shift nulls, family-wise thresholds, BH q-values, and a purged walk-forward logistic model vs baselines.
findings: Data: front-month MNQ, 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31 only (~3 months, unadjusted, one roll MNQZ5->MNQH6 2025-12-16). Bars: 1m=86,925, 1h=1,451, 4h=394 (study_run_information in E:/lake-workspace/mnq_indicator_study.duckdb; datalake/notebooks/mnq_talib_1m.py:67-84). Datasets derived/mnq_talib_{1m,1h,4h}/recipe=talib_v1.

No output is saved in the notebook (session json empty). The recorded run is in .remember/today-2026-08-03.done.md: cost 0.70 pts, 6-fold CV, stickiness 0.441-0.454 (published 0.452), OOS Sharpe 1.554 (published single-split 1.32), regime-1-only gate Sharpe 1.668 vs baseline 1.595, and 'Sharpe improvement CI [-6e-6, 1e-6] ~0; not viable'.

The stickiness assert (line 164) demands mean transition diagonal > 1.3x chance (0.25), i.e. > 0.325; recorded 0.441-0.454, so regimes persist. That is a volatility-clustering fact, not a directional edge.

Verdict rule (line 294): 'trade' a regime if the BCa lower bound of mean per-bar net return > 0. Gated Sharpe difference has a per-bar-effect CI straddling 0 (recorded), so the notebook itself concludes: do not ship the gate.

(2) Per-regime 'trade/sit_out' verdicts (lines 281-299) and the gating evaluation (lines 314-326) are computed on the same full tagged sample, i.e. selected and scored on identical bars, not walk-forward. (3) The crossover pair 5/100 was chosen in-sample from a 966-combo grid (FINDINGS.md:441), so the 'OOS' fold Sharpe is not OOS for the rule parameters. topic: Path-geometry (efficiency ratio / regression shape) as predictors; direction-label alignment

Section 5 uses generate_direction_labels on the same closes, H=60/10.

topic: Rolling linear-regression slope as a trading signal (MNQ 5m)
purpose: Computes 10/20/50-bar rolling OLS slope of price, trades sign(slope) with an adaptive threshold, and backtests against buy-and-hold with a per-change cost.
data_sources: Lake view ohlcv_5m, symbol MNQ, timestamp >= 2025-09-25 (18,405 bars to 2025-12-30; verified by SQL). Bounded to ~3 months on 2026-08-31, so stored .ipynb numbers no longer apply.
methods: scipy linregress slope of raw close in points/bar, rolling-200 std threshold x0.3 -> +1/-1/0, signal shifted one bar, log-return PnL, cost 1.4 pts per signal change, Sharpe with 252*78 bars/yr.
findings: I re-ran the notebook logic on the same 18,405 5m bars (read-only SQL + pandas; notebook not executed): signal shares long 36.9% / short 30.1% / flat 33.0%; 1,619 signal changes over 18,386 bars.

Gross log return +0.0278 (Sharpe 0.35), buy-and-hold +0.0359 (Sharpe 0.40); net of the notebook's 1.4 pt cost per change: -0.0616 (Sharpe -0.77, -5.98%). Gross P&L +713 pts vs cost 2,267 pts (1,619 x 1.4).

Position segments (constant-position runs, entry at first-bar close to exit): 816 segments, win rate 36.8%, average win 52.4 pts, average loss 29.4 pts (ratio 1.78:1), summed 575 pts before cost - the shape of a trend-follower (below 40% wins, near 2:1), but the edge is fully consumed by costs at this trade frequency.
Bar-level 'win rate' (46.9% of nonzero bars) is not a trade win rate and is not comparable to the 40% target.
lookahead_detail: Signal is shifted one bar before use (slope_analysis.py:369), slope and rolling-200 std are trailing. The slope is in absolute points per bar (price-level dependent), which the workspace normalisation rule disallows as a model input; the adaptive rolling-std threshold partially masks it. No centred windows.
edge_summary: Gross Sharpe 0.35 vs buy-and-hold 0.40 over ~3 months (one regime), net Sharpe -0.77 after 1.4 pt per change. Segment-level payoff is 36.8% wins with 1.78:1 win/loss before costs, which looks like a trend profile but is not net-profitable and is one 3-month in-sample window.
validity_issues: Single 3-month window, no walk-forward, no holdout; parameters (window 20, multiplier 0.3) were fixed a priori but not tested for sensitivity.

Cost handling is inconsistent: 1.4 pts is charged once per signal change, so flat<->position (one side) is overcharged and long<->short reversal (two sides) is undercharged; no slippage model beyond the constant; uses 1.4 pts not the AMP $1.78 fee + measured slippage decomposition.
Sharpe annualisation assumes 78 five-minute bars per day but the series is ~23h globex (18,405 bars in ~68 sessions), so Sharpe is mis-scaled.
Trades are opened on the next bar's return, i.e. fills at the signal-bar close are assumed with no delay.
Slope in points is price-level dependent.
Buy-and-hold uses raw close of an unadjusted contract series; roll gaps are not handled in the returns.
reusable_assets: None worth keeping beyond the idea of a rolling-OLS trend gate; a normalised version already exists as path_geometry.py rolling t-beta and analytics/trend/trend_state.py (TrendState).
recommendation: Do not use as a signal. The one thing worth carrying forward is the payoff shape: trend-following on 5m gives ~37% wins with ~1.8:1 win/loss, so 40% win / 2:1 payoff is a plausible target profile for a trend/breakout entry with a wide-stop, but only at far lower turnover (cost per trade must be a small fraction of the ~52-pt average win). Any multimodal design must drive trade count down and gate entries, then evaluate with the AMP cost decomposition, not this 1.4-pt per-change charge.

topic: PCA and HNSW explainer on the Model Lens vector space
purpose: Teaches what PC1/PC2 and HNSW nearest-neighbour search are, using the 4,000-bar, 19/32-dimensional Lens study landed in the lake.
data_sources: s3://derived/recipe=lens_vector_space_study/ tables component_spectrum, component_loadings, neighbour_index_recall, standardized_features (MNQ, 4,000 bars from the multimodal run). Built by model/scripts/build_vector_space_study.py.
methods: Interactive angle slider on two z-scored features, term-by-term variance sum, scree/cumulative curves, loadings by block, a greedy layered-graph walk on 220 real bars, recall@12 vs ef_search.
findings: Continuous basis: PC1 24.24%, PC2 17.23%, PC3 15.81%; PC1+PC2 = 41.47% (verified by SQL on component_spectrum). Full basis: PC1 18.64%, PC1+PC2 32.46%, top-3 43.26%.

HNSW recall@12: continuous basis 0.9972 at ef_search 8 then 1.0 from ef_search 16; full basis 0.9986 at 8, 1.0 from 16 (verified by SQL). Notebook prose says 100% 'from ef_search 32 up' (line 829) - actual threshold is 16; the mean query time is about 1-2 ms for both HNSW and brute force, so at 4,000 bars the index gives no speed-up.
In the full basis pattern_multihot (13 of 32 dims) dominates PC1 by dimension count, which is why the continuous basis (19 dims, no pattern block) is the default.
lookahead_detail: Explainer only; features are the run's already z-scored blocks. Standardisation is 'over the run', i.e. a whole-run statistic, which is acceptable for a visualisation but would leak if used to build model inputs.
edge_summary: No predictive claim; it explains the vector-space visualisation. The one useful fact is that the 19-dim continuous token space needs more than two axes (41.5% in PC1+PC2).
validity_issues: Prose thresholds slightly stale (ef_search 32 vs measured 16).
Full-run z-scoring is a whole-series statistic.
Needs the vss DuckDB extension and lake S3 credentials in env to run.
recommendation: Use only as documentation for the Lens/nearest-neighbour panel. For retrieval over bar tokens (e.g. an evidence/analog bank) note that exact search is as fast as HNSW at this scale, and that price levels must stay out of any distance (the workspace rule) - the continuous basis (no pattern one-hot dominance) is the safer space.

topic: Volatility value to price range/dollar conversion, calibration and timeframe scaling law
purpose: Shows that a log(high-low) volatility value converts exactly to points/ticks/USD (exp(v) x $2/pt), measures the mean-vs-median (Jensen) bias, empirical calibration by EWMA volatility decile, and a sqrt-of-time law across 1m/5m/15m/30m/45m/1h.
data_sources: Lake via analytics core.lake.load_ohlcv_tf, MNQ, six timeframes, 2025-09-25 onward (~3 months, to 2025-12-30). Spot-checked by SQL: 1m n=92,025 median range 6.75 pts / mean 9.22; 15m n=6,135 median 26.25 / mean 36.46; 1h n=1,536 median 53.25 / mean 74.17 - all match CLAUDE.md.
methods: generate_volatility_labels (zero-range masked), causal RiskMetrics EWMA lambda 0.94 forecast, decile calibration of exp(bin forecast) vs realised next-bar range, residual-sigma lognormal factor vs measured mean/median, log-log power-law fit range ~ T^H, nine-number statistics per series.
findings: Median high-low travel per contract, 1m/5m/15m/30m/45m/1h: 6.75 / 15.00 / 26.25 / 37.25 / 46.00 / 53.25 pts = $13.50 / 30 / 52.5 / 74.5 / 92 / 106.5 (CLAUDE.md table; 1m, 15m, 1h re-verified by SQL).
Log-range is near-normal (excess kurtosis -0.13..-0.31 at all six timeframes) while raw range is fat-tailed (skew 2.3-3.6, kurtosis 7.7-31.9), which licenses the log conversion.
exp(EWMA forecast) runs above the realised median by +3.4% (5m) to +6.7% (45m) median bias (CLAUDE.md, stored notebook outputs).
The Gaussian factor exp(s^2/2) understates the measured mean/median by 3.9% (1m) rising to 9.0% (45m) because bin residuals are heavy-tailed (median bin excess kurtosis 78 at 1m).
Range scales as T^0.5049 (R^2 0.99995) and mean log-range as T^0.5163 (R^2 0.99997); sd(log-range) varies only 0.697-0.746 across a 60x change in bar length; one conversion serves all timeframes.
Residual sigma of EWMA forecast grows 0.418 (1m) to 0.607 (45m): forecast quality does not transfer, the outcome band widens with bar size.
lookahead_detail: EWMA forecast is causal (forecast[t] is paired with label_next[t] = bar t+1). Ladders and power-law fits are descriptive whole-window statistics over the same ~3 months, used only for conversion tables, not as trading features. Zero-range bars are masked rather than floored.
edge_summary: No directional or PnL edge is claimed or tested. It is a sizing/scaling tool: it converts a volatility forecast into a stop/target distance in points and dollars per timeframe, with measured median, mean and 10-90% outcome bands. The underlying volatility forecastability (HAR-RV/GBT skill over HAR, RLS +0.7 R2) is documented elsewhere and is the only strong predictive signal found on this instrument.
validity_issues: Single 3-month window (2025-09-25..2025-12-30), one regime; bias figures come from a naive EWMA forecast, not the eventual model's forecast.
Point-based ladders are price-level dependent; use median_pct for cross-period comparison.
Calibration deciles at 45m/1h have only ~153-207 bars per bin.
reusable_assets: Measured ladder: median USD per volatility percentile x timeframe (notebook section 3)
recommendation: Use this as the sizing layer of the multimodal system: a volatility head predicts log-range, the ladder converts it to a stop and target in points, and the 2:1 reward-to-risk is set as target = 2 x stop with the stop taken from a high quantile (not exp(v), which is the median bar). Use the measured mean/median factor, not the Gaussian one, and re-derive the bias for the final model's own forecasts on the holdout.

topic: Candlestick pattern CNN trained on synthetic TA-Lib-verified windows, tested on real MNQ 2024+ (encoder for tokenisation)
purpose: Reports per-pattern AUC/average precision of a CNN that recognises the 61 TA-Lib candle patterns, ROC/decile calibration per pattern, example TP/FP/FN candles and a PCA of the 256-d embedding.
data_sources: chart_cnn/synth/runs/seed0/{real_test_results.csv, real_test_pred.npz} and chart_cnn/data/test_real.parquet: 126,624 real MNQ 5m windows 2024-01-01..2025-12-30 (55 targets), never trained on. Training data: synthetic samples built from 2019-2023 seeds (gen_synthetic.py, 200,000 per pattern).
methods: Multi-label CNN on GPU-rendered pattern-only images, loss masked to patterns visible in the bars drawn; checkpoint chosen on synthetic-validation mean AUC (train_synth_cnn.py:109), not on the real test set; labels are TA-Lib outputs.
findings: Computed from real_test_results.csv: 61 patterns, 54 scoreable; mean AUC 0.9887, median 0.9963, 52 of 54 above 0.95, weakest CDLSHORTLINE 0.840, CDLBREAKAWAY 0.917 (3 positives), CDLHANGINGMAN 0.961, CDLHAMMER 0.966. 7 patterns have zero real positives in 2024+ (e.g. CDL3STARSINSOUTH, CDLABANDONEDBABY, CDLKICKING).
Training log (synth/train_synth_cnn.py log, epoch 5): synth-val mean AUC 0.9968, real-test mean AUC 0.9887, min 0.840.
Several patterns have very few positives (CDL2CROWS 4, CDLCOUNTERATTACK 1), so their 0.997-1.0 AUCs are not meaningful.
The task is agreement with a deterministic arithmetic function (TA-Lib), not a market target; high AUC shows the CNN sees candle shape, nothing about profitability.
lookahead_detail: Windows are 1-5 bar trailing candle shapes labelled by TA-Lib on the same bars; there is no forward label. Checkpoint selection uses synthetic validation, not the real test.
edge_summary: No trading or predictive edge is measured; the notebook shows the CNN reproduces TA-Lib pattern flags on real 2024-25 bars (mean AUC 0.989). Whether any pattern flag predicts returns is answered only by the direction notebooks (null, see report.py).
validity_issues: Target is a deterministic function of the input bars, so the CNN adds nothing over calling TA-Lib for detection; its value is only as a learned embedding.
Rare patterns have too few positives for meaningful AUC.
Requires torch, gpu_render and the run artifacts; artifacts are stored in the repo.
recommendation: Possible image/pattern modality encoder for the multimodal model, but the arithmetic pattern flags and the 12-dim candle embedding already carry this information exactly; use the CNN embedding only if an ablation shows lift over the plain 13-flag multi-hot on net PnL. Do not expect edge from it.

topic: Chart-image CNN vs 1D sequence CNN for barrier-direction prediction (MNQ 1m/5m/1h)
purpose: Out-of-sample report on whether 48-bar chart-image shape predicts which +/-2 ATR barrier is hit first, with a 1D-sequence control, decile calibration and mean R by predicted decile.
data_sources: chart_cnn/pkg/cnn_results.csv and pred_<tag>.npz built by build.py/train.py from MNQ parquet (mnq1m step-3 thinned n=93,777 test; mnq5m n=187,849; mnq1h n=15,638). Split: first 60% train (last 15% of that for early stopping), last 40% test, chronological; test years not stated in code (full history to 2025).
methods: Label: +/-B*ATR (B=2, ATR14 EWM) barrier first-hit within a time cap of 4 x median ZigZag leg, timeout -> sign of return; images 94x144 binary; 2D CNN vs 1D CNN; AUC, mean R of top 20% long and bottom 20% short predictions vs naive long.
findings: From cnn_results.csv - test AUC: 1m 2D 0.5042 / 1D 0.5058; 5m 2D 0.5050 / 1D 0.5062; 1h 2D 0.4982 / 1D 0.5052. All are below the notebook's own 0.53 'no signal' bar (report.py:53-57).
The 1D sequence control equals or beats the 2D image model at every timeframe on AUC and (except 1h) on R, so any signal is in the numbers, not the chart shape.

Costs are not included: at 5m one ATR is roughly 21 points or more (mean bar range 20.8 pts), so a 1.4-pt round trip is about 0.07 R, which equals or exceeds the +0.047..+0.066 R top-quintile expectancy; at 1m ATR is about 9 pts so cost is about 0.15 R against +0.04..+0.05 R.
lookahead_detail: Images use bars <= t and are scaled to their own window (README rules). Concerns: (1) the time cap tcap = 4 x median ZigZag leg is computed from the whole series (build.py:9), a whole-series statistic entering the label definition; (2) no purge between the 60% train cut and the test block though labels reach up to tcap bars forward (train.py cut = int(len*0.6), no gap); (3) ATR-based R for timeouts uses close[t+cap]. Side-effect: top-20% quantile thresholds are taken from the test predictions themselves (train.py:hi = pp >= np.quantile(pp,.8)), a test-set-derived gate (same defect the workspace already records for simulate_trades).
edge_summary: AUC 0.498-0.506 on 15k-188k out-of-sample bars for both image and sequence models; top-quintile R of +0.04..+0.07 ATR is gross of cost, uses a test-derived threshold, overlaps heavily between adjacent samples (no CI reported) and is not distinguishable from naive-long drift plus noise. Image shape adds nothing over the 1D control.
validity_issues: No confidence intervals or effective-sample-size correction despite heavily overlapping labels.
Gross of costs; quantile gate derived from test predictions.
Only a single 60/40 split, no walk-forward.
1m result uses --step 3 thinning (n=93,777), which still leaves highly dependent samples.
Long expectancy compared to naive long in a rising market (MNQ 7.7k to 25.9k).
reusable_assets: E:/source/repos/ml_dashboard/Trading/quant/chart_cnn/pkg/label.py (ATR14, ATR-scaled ZigZag, symmetric barrier label returning R)
recommendation: Take from it the negative result: chart-image shape has AUC about 0.505 with an identical 1D control, so do not build the multimodal model around a direction-from-image head. The barrier-in-ATR-units label with R payoff is useful for defining a 2:1 target (barrier B=2 ATR gives +2R/-1... note symmetric here, so use asymmetric 2:1 barriers), evaluated with a causal threshold and costs.

topic: Can the image CNN see candle shape? (positive control for the direction null)
purpose: Shows the same image CNN recognises 17 hand-built arithmetic candle patterns almost perfectly, so the ~0.50 direction AUC is a statement about the market rather than model capacity.
data_sources: chart_cnn/pkg/pattern_results_mnq5m.csv and pred_patterns_mnq5m.npz (MNQ 5m; last 40% of windows, never trained on); 17 patterns such as doji, hammer, engulfing, inside_bar, morning_star.
methods: Same images/network as report.py, but labels are deterministic arithmetic functions of the last 1-3 bars; per-pattern AUC, average precision vs prevalence, ROC and decile hit-rate.
findings: Computed from pattern_results_mnq5m.csv: mean AUC 0.9804 over 17 patterns, range 0.928 (evening_star) to 0.998 (wide_range_bar); average precision is weakest for the rare 3-bar patterns (morning_star 0.286, evening_star 0.236, three_crows 0.379, three_soldiers 0.402).
Prevalences span 0.8% (three_crows) to 17.3% (spinning_top); AP far exceeds prevalence everywhere.
Interpretation stated in the notebook: near-1.0 pattern AUC combined with 0.505 direction AUC (report.py) means shape is fully visible but not predictive.
lookahead_detail: Labels are functions of bars <= t; no forward information.
edge_summary: No trading edge; it is a positive control confirming the CNN can see the same shapes that carry no direction information.
validity_issues: Chronological last-40% test set, single split; the label is a deterministic function so high AUC says nothing about markets.
Some pattern windows (morning/evening star) have low AP, i.e. weak detection of rare 3-bar shapes.
recommendation: Use as the justification for dropping image-to-direction heads: the encoder is competent, the target is not there. Candle-pattern information should enter the multimodal model as cheap arithmetic flags/embedding blocks, not as a learned image head.

topic: TA-indicator and conditional TA-Lib strategies on MNQ/NQ vs a 600 ticks/day goal (model rounds, rule search, level quality, pre-registered confirmation, frequency round 4)
purpose: Dashboard for the study in docs/ta-strategy-600-ticks.md. Reads derived_ta_strategy_600_ticks_*, derived_ta_rule_strategies_600_ticks_*, derived_ta_conditional_strategies_600_ticks_* (rounds, configurations, folds, daily, trades, oracle_by_session, reviews, strategies, level_quality, templates, confirmation_*, frequency_*). Contains a steppable win-rate-needed formula, per-configuration bars with 95% block-bootstrap intervals, alpha after buy-and-hold beta, matched-random-entry nulls, and per-column small multiples. It is the most decision-relevant notebook of the ten because it is the only one that measures net trading results after AMP costs.
data_sources: MNQ 2019-05/06..2025-12 (walk-forward tests 2021-07..2025-12 for model rounds; tuning on prior years, test years 2022-2025 for conditional rounds); NQ 2010-06-07..2019-05-31 (2,306 sessions, never used for tuning); bars 1m/5m/15m/30m/1h/4h from ohlcv_full_<tf> back-adjusted at rolls (cycle.rolls). Costs from packages/config/cost_model.json: $1.39/side = $0.89 fees + 1 tick slippage; 5.56 ticks round trip; +1 tick on stopped exits.
methods: Model rounds: logistic and LightGBM direction classifiers on a TA-Lib battery, fixed-hold, gate on conviction, next-open fills via cycle/simulate.py, scored per session day with Newey-West alpha over buy-and-hold beta, White Reality Check, deflated Sharpe. topic: FinBERT news sentiment feature family (nine finbert_* columns) and its decay formula
purpose: Explores headlines from RSS, Alpha Vantage and GDELT scored by ProsusAI/finbert, routed to instruments, and turned into nine decayed-sum features via lake.sentiment (datalake repo src/lake/sentiment.py) on any bar grid. The stated rule (Tyler 2026-09-27) is that FinBERT columns go into every model.
data_sources: lake.news / lake.sentiment over curated/news_articles, curated/news_sentiment, curated/news_coverage plus the hub spool data/live/spool/curated. Default window is the last 3 UTC days (live data since 2026-09-28). Landed history in the lake: derived_news_features (recipe finbert_v1, 1m) covers 2025-12-15 to 2025-12-21 only for MNQ (20,700 rows), MES (6,900), M2K (6,794), MYM (6,814); curated news_articles has 48,270 rows 2025-12-15T00:15 to 2026-09-28T23:49 (SQL run).
methods: S(t) = sum over headlines known strictly before bar open of weight*score*2^(-(t-a_i)/h); weight = relevance x direction, syndicated copies collapsed inside 2 hours, GDELT known at crawl bucket +15 min; h_short = max(20 min, 4 bars), h_long = max(1440 min, 32 bars); signed log transform. Nine columns: decayed short/long sentiment, news intensity, burst ratio, mean-window sentiment, log article count, log minutes since last article, macro sentiment, coverage flag.
findings: Coverage: derived_news_features holds one week (2025-12-15..21) of 1m rows per root; docs/finbert.md states a 2025-08-01..12-30 MNQ 5m run had news on 4.8% of bars and 2,811 MNQ articles (one GDELT week). The rest of the 2025 holdout (2025-07-01..12-31) has coverage flag 0 on about 95% of bars.

Data-quality: MNQ has 20,700 rows in derived_news_features versus about 6,800-6,900 for each other root over the same 7 days (about 3x), suggesting duplicated landings; dedupe before any join (SQL count grouped by root).

The notebook computes no relationship between sentiment and returns; it documents distributions and the decay mechanics only. The only measurement cited is a half-life choice from datalake CLAUDE.md (MNQ 1m, 2025-12-15..22: 30-60 min windows keep 2-2.6x the dispersion of 240 min).
GDELT backfill 2024-01..now was stalled (GDELT refused the address 2026-09-28), so history for training does not exist yet.
lookahead_detail: Designed causally: articles count only if known strictly before bar open (seen_ts, not published_ts; GDELT +15 min; earliest UTC instant at DST edges). Residual risks: futures bars stamp Pacific wall-clock as UTC and are relocalised in lake.sentiment (mistakes there would leak up to 7-8 hours in either direction); notebook line 172 uses np.arange(...) with min(time.time()) so window is live-clipped; syndicated-title collapse depends on first-copy time.
edge_summary: No predictive test exists: the notebook shows feature distributions only, and there is only one week of overlap with price (2025-12-15..21, about 5 sessions), far too small to estimate any effect; live data collection began 2026-09-28 so the multimodal model's text modality cannot be trained or validated on a 2025-07..12 holdout.
validity_issues: One week of history versus 6.5 years of bars; the text modality is unlearnable on the historical set.
No return-relationship test; no significance.
Routing relevance scores and FinBERT's financial-news domain shift to futures headlines are unvalidated.
Possible duplicate landings in derived_news_features for MNQ.
reusable_assets: live/ hub (python -m live) for forward collection
recommendation: Keep the nine finbert_* columns as the text modality's fixed interface, but plan the backtest without it: train and holdout-test the price/flow modalities on the 2019-2025 data, add FinBERT only as a forward-tested (paper-trading from 2026-09-28) or ablation feature with the coverage flag. Do not report any FinBERT importance over 2025 as evidence; measure its incremental value only after the GDELT backfill lands, and dedupe derived_news_features first.

topic: FX spread economics, cross-pair correlation, in-sample feature screen with best-of-N block-permutation null
purpose: Reads CSVs written by scripts/pair_spread.py, pair_correlation.py, pair_structure.py and reports what each of 18 FX pairs costs, how many independent bets exist, and which price-structure features survive a family-wise null. No computation in the notebook itself.
data_sources: 18 spot FX pairs, 1m bars 2020-01-01 to 2026-08-26 from Iceberg market.bars (95_pair_inventory.csv: 43,812,773 bars). Two-sided bid/ask exists only on 9.6%-22.1% of rows, all after 2026-01-05 (first_quote 2026-01-05). Screen is 15m/1h/1d, 50 features per pair-timeframe (111 distinct feature names), targets forward_log_return and forward_log_range (results/103_structure_screen.csv, 5,400 tests). Correlation at 5m/1h/1d (99, 101). No MNQ.
methods: Median spread in pips and basis points, per UTC hour, spread/ATR(14) by timeframe; raw, residual (currency-factor) and tail-decile correlation, eigen participation ratio; Spearman of each feature vs next-bar target, best-of-N null = max |rho| over the feature set under 500 one-trading-day block permutations of the target, feature must beat 95th percentile; redundancy Spearman between features.
findings: Measured median EURUSD spread is 1.6 pips = 1.38 bp; USDJPY 1.6 pips = 1.02 bp (cheapest), NZDJPY 2.96 bp and GBPAUD 2.76 bp (dearest). Source: results/96_pair_spread.csv (median of spread_basis_points_median). This is double the 0.6-0.8 pip cost assumed in notebooks 01-15.
Spread by UTC hour is flat (median 1.80-1.90 bp for hours 0-20) then 7.77 bp at hour 21 (about 4.1x) and 2.37 bp at hour 22. Source: 97_pair_spread_hour.csv median across pairs.
spread/ATR(14) for EURUSD is 1.191 at 1m, 0.490 at 5m, 0.268 at 15m, 0.125 at 1h, 0.061 at 4h, 0.025 at 1d; best pair USDJPY 0.892 at 1m and 0.090 at 1h. Source: 98_pair_tradability.csv.

Correlation participation ratio (effective independent bets among 18 pairs): raw 4.26 (1d), 4.32 (1h), 4.48 (5m); residual 8.60, 6.50, 9.78. Mean absolute raw pairwise correlation 0.35-0.36, tail-decile 0.52-0.62. Source: 101_correlation_eigen.csv, 99_pair_correlation.csv.

Family-wise survival: 923 of 2,700 forward_log_range tests survive (34.2%, max |spearman| 0.740, log_range/shape family) versus 508 of 2,700 forward_log_return tests (18.8%, max |spearman| 0.0767, AUDJPY 1d volume_zscore_20). Source: 103_structure_screen.csv (recomputed).

Strongest direction survivors are close_position_in_range at 15m/1h on EURCHF/EURGBP/GBPCHF with spearman -0.066 to -0.073 vs null_95 0.007-0.022 (mean reversion of same-bar close location). Source: 103_structure_screen.csv.

Volume family survives 100% of range tests at 15m and 1h (108/108) but the script header states about 59% of the tick-count/volatility correlation is hour-of-day and the hour-matched null 'has not been run'. Source: scripts/pair_structure.py lines 33-47.
lookahead_detail: Targets are (logc.shift(-1)-logc) and next-bar high/low range (scripts/pair_structure.py:219-220), forward-looking by design; features are same-bar. The screen ranks the whole sample at once, so it is a descriptive screen, not a fitted model. Not a look-ahead in a trading rule, but the result cannot be used as a forecast estimate.
validity_issues: Screen is in-sample on the entire 2020-2026 history: no train/test or walk-forward split, so spearman values are not out-of-sample estimates.
Null permutes one-trading-day blocks and preserves the diurnal cycle of both series, so anything sharing hour-of-day survives (script header admits this); hour-matched null not run.
5,400 tests on heavily autocorrelated series; survivors overlap across pairs/timeframes (18 pairs have effective 4-10 independent bets).
Direction 'survival' of 18.8% contradicts the chart title 'direction is not forecastable' in the sense that survivors exist, but the largest |spearman| is 0.077 and no cost is applied.
Spreads are OANDA retail quotes from Jan-Aug 2026 only, extrapolated nowhere but applied to no PnL; notebook 19 cells read CSVs that must exist in results/.
edge_summary: Volatility is predictable (up to |rho| 0.74 same-bar range persistence, 34% of tests survive) but that is a level/persistence effect, not a trading edge. For direction the largest in-sample Spearman is 0.077 and typical survivors are 0.02-0.07; my back-of-envelope (not in the notebook) is a sign-position gross gain of about 0.8*rho*sigma per bar (about 0.06 sigma) versus a one-way spread of 0.19 ATR at 1h for EURCHF, so it would not pay. No costs or PnL are applied in the notebook.
recommendation: Reuse the measured-spread and spread/ATR method (apply to MNQ as ticks/commission over ATR per timeframe) and the best-of-N block-permutation screen, but run it walk-forward with an hour-of-day-matched null. Do not read the forex 'survivors' as signals; use the finding that cost per unit of movement collapses with horizon to justify longer holding periods and fewer, larger trades for a 2:1 target.

findings: Peak excess entropy is 0.030 bits at 1m (0.56% of 5.42 bits), 0.005 at 5m, 0.0042 at 15m, 0.0057 at 1h, 0.0108 at 4h, 0.0266 at 1d (cell 4).
96 patterns survive discovery and confirmation, all at 1m, length 3-4, max order-1 lift 3.17 (S14- S12- S14+ S14+, count 34, support about 6e-4 for the strongest).
Survivors are built from S14 (one-tick minute, near-pure body): 2.37x over-represented at 21:00-22:00 UTC and 0.48x at 14:00 UTC, mean range_z -0.22 vs -0.04 (cell 11).
At 5m and coarser the tests are mostly untestable for sample size (1h: 22,440 positions vs 117,649 possible 3-grams).

Surviving patterns are a liquidity artefact of one-tick minutes in thin hours.

topic: Do candle-shape patterns forecast direction, and does it pay after spread
purpose: Tests 1-5 word patterns against the unconditional up-rate with BH FDR, holdout sign retention, net-of-cost trading, and a continuous-coordinate logistic benchmark.
data_sources: EURUSD 1m-1d, horizons 1,2,3,5,10 bars; discovery on leading 75% of the 80% dev slice, confirmation on trailing 25%; sealed 20% never read.
methods: Exact binomial vs base rate, Benjamini-Hochberg, out-of-sample sign hold rate, position from pattern-bar close held for the horizon, 0.8-pip retail round trip, breakeven spread, logistic on raw (upper, body, lower).
findings: 255 of 301 significant patterns keep their sign on the confirmation slice (84.7%); n=1 accounts for 212 of 255 holds (n=1: 255 significant, 212 holds; n=2: 40/37; n=3: 6/6).
Break-even spread: median 0.033 pips, best 0.284 pips vs real 0.6-1.0 retail / 0.1-0.2 institutional; every configuration net-negative.
Continuous-coordinate logistic AUC 0.50-0.52 (1m n=1 mean 0.5024, max 0.5061; 4h 0.4943-0.5094; 1d max 0.5300).
Edges are mean reversion: down-closing words followed by up-moves; best single-pattern hit rate 0.566 (S04- S05-, 129 confirm cases, edge +0.1155).
lookahead_detail: Return is measured from the close of the pattern-completing bar t forward (forecast.forward_return), so entry assumes a fill at that close; no next-open delay. Cost-per-turn 0.8 pip. Horizon crossing data gaps is discarded.
validity_issues: Confirmation slice lies inside the dev region; the sealed 20% was never scored, so no true holdout.
1m mean reversion from down-closing to up moves may include bid-ask/microstructure bounce; gross Sharpe 2.4 with 0.014-pip breakeven is not tradable.
301 significant patterns out of thousands tested; hold rate 84.7% is measured on overlapping, autocorrelated 1m bars.
Fixed 0.8-pip cost; later measured OANDA median is 1.6 pips.
edge_summary: Real but tiny mean-reversion information (hit rates 0.505-0.566 gross), 20-50x too small to clear the spread: median breakeven spread 0.033 pips, best 0.284 pips; every configuration net-negative; logistic AUC 0.50-0.52.
recommendation: Confirms candle shape alone cannot support a 40% / 2:1 strategy. Use candle shape only as a low-weight contextual feature; the notebook's own suggestion (trade only when expected move is large relative to spread) is the actionable lever.

data_sources: EURUSD, 4 timeframes (1m,5m,15m,1h), 3 context lengths, 2 horizons = 120 fits; fit on leading 75% of dev, scored on trailing 25%; sealed 20% never read.
methods: Logistic regression on the last n bars; AUC on held-out block; softmax temperature check.
findings: Mean held-out AUC: soft 0.5111, onehot 0.5110, continuous 0.5108, geometric 0.5108, pmi_svd 0.5100; spread between representations 0.0011 versus 0.0410 within (36x) (cells 3-4).
Context 1/3/5 bars: AUC 0.5094-0.5119 for every representation; more context does not help (cell 6).
Soft encoding at T=0.005 has top weight 0.86-0.89 and about 1.4 effective words; T=0.05 gave soft AUC 0.5105 vs 0.5111 (cell 8).
lookahead_detail: Train/test in chronological order inside dev; encoder fit on the training leading 75%.
validity_issues: AUC about 0.51 is essentially chance; the comparison is between representations of a near-null signal, and a weak probe by design.
Held-out block is the trailing 25% of dev only; sealed tail not used.
edge_summary: AUC 0.510-0.511 for every encoding, differences 0.001, well below any spread hurdle (06 shows AUC needed above 0.53-0.59 with costs).
recommendation: Encoding choice is irrelevant; use continuous or geometric 4-dim shape inputs, initialise any learned embedding from centroids, and do not add a sequence model over candle words.

topic: Candle-word transition matrix, lift, forecasts and cost of the strongest pairs
purpose: Table of P(next|current) with lift, mutual information/Cramer's V, FDR-tested directional forecasts of 2-word pairs, and net-of-cost trade test.
data_sources: EURUSD 49-symbol word+direction alphabet at 1m/5m/15m/1h; 9,132 ordered pairs observed; discovery 75% / confirmation 25% inside dev; 1m has 1,279,630 pairs.
methods: Transition lift with confirmation lift; per-row KL; Cramer's V; directional edge with FDR + held-out sign; trade test at 1m.
findings: Strongest transitions have lift about 2.0 and replicate: S21- to S06- lift 2.03/2.15 (count 643); S06- to S14- 1.94/1.94 (count 1,815) (cell 5).
Mean per-row KL is 0.0115 bits at 1m, 0.0111 at 5m, 0.0279 at 15m, 0.113 at 1h against about 5.4 bits total; Cramer's V 0.017-0.047.
25 of 10,309 tested pairs survive FDR plus held-out sign; strongest edges up to about -10.6 points, mostly pairs ending in S14+ predicting down (mean reversion) (cell 9).
Trading those at 1m h=1 (20 transitions): gross hit 55.96%, gross Sharpe 2.01, net Sharpe -50.6, breakeven 0.0178 pips, exposure 0.62%; h=3 gross Sharpe 0.93 net -26.2 (cell 11).
lookahead_detail: Same discovery/confirmation protocol as 06; entry from the close of the completing bar.
validity_issues: 10,309 candidate pairs, only 25 survive; small gross edges concentrated at 1m where tick-size and bounce effects dominate.
Confirmation is inside dev; sealed tail unscored; cost fixed 0.8 pip.
edge_summary: Replicating short-horizon mean reversion (hit 55.96% gross at 1m h=1) but breakeven spread 0.018 pips versus 0.6-1.0 retail, so net Sharpe -50.6. Information is under 1.5% of symbol entropy.
recommendation: Do not pursue candle transitions as an alpha source. It reinforces that any edge in 1-minute price shape is roughly two orders of magnitude below cost; target holding periods where move/cost is high.

topic: Volatility-scaled triple-barrier labelling and its baselines
purpose: Defines the label used for supervised trading models and measures what it does on raw EURUSD before any signal: gambler's-ruin baseline, shuffled surrogate, intrabar vs close-only touch, time-limit and ratio sweep, clock dependence.
data_sources: EURUSD 2,208,215 1m bars and all 7 timeframes; outcomes in results/48-52 (175 labellings in the grid), max_bars 20, 2:1 target:stop, box in trailing-60-bar volatility units.
methods: labels.triple_barrier with touch='extreme' (high/low) or 'close'; within-run shuffled surrogate; 5 target multiples x 5 time limits; target share per UTC hour under volatility vs fixed box.
findings: At 2:1 a driftless walk reaches the target first 33.33% of the time (1/(1+2)); EURUSD long target share is 33.42% at 1m, 28.96% at 4h and 21.43% at 1d; excess over the shuffled surrogate ranges -2.32 (15m) to +1.06 (1d) points and changes sign.

Close-only labelling reports +0.125 to +0.148 vol units per trade at every timeframe versus +0.039 at 1m, +0.003 at 5m and negative from 15m up with intrabar touch; the apparent edge is stops not recorded.
Positive rate at 5m with 20-bar limit: 60% at 0.5:1, 49% at 1:1, 34% at 2:1, 28% at 3:1 (label balance is set by the ratio).
20-bar limit fires on 0.35%-4.63% of intraday trades and 0.00% at 4h/1d; going 20 to 80 bars moves target share +0.3 pt at 1m and +2.3 pt at 15m. Median trade held 1-3 bars.
Volatility box spans 8.5 points of target share across the day vs 13.8 for a fixed box at 1m, but 7.5 vs 6.0 at 1h (60-bar window too long).
lookahead_detail: Labels are forward-looking by design and entered at the close of a finished bar; the box uses trailing volatility. Same-bar target-and-stop is settled as a loss ("both" bucket 0.87% at 5m).
validity_issues: No signal or cost included ('Nothing here is a signal').
max_bars=20 is an unexamined default (written 2026-08-18 per the notebook).
edge_summary: No edge: a passive long entry hits a 2:1 target 33.4% (1m) versus 33.3% random-walk baseline; largest excess over shuffle is +1.06 points. For the 40% / 2:1 goal a strategy must add about 6.7 points of hit rate over this baseline (my derivation: expectancy at 40%/2:1 is +0.2R before costs; breakeven is 33.3%).
recommendation: Adopt this labelling (intrabar touch, volatility-scaled box, separate 'gap' and 'time' outcomes, resolution_bars, MFE/MAE) for MNQ, measured against the 33.3% baseline and a shuffled surrogate. Scale the box by a window shorter than the seasonality it removes, and add session-gap handling.

topic: Nineteen rule-based trend definitions scored net of cost with shuffle surrogate
purpose: Draw and unit-check EMA cross, Donchian, slope and swing definitions, prove causality, and score them on EURUSD net of a 0.6-pip spread with a bootstrap Sharpe interval and shuffled-bar surrogate.
methods: Position +1/0/-1 at close of t earning t to t+1; 18 assertions on the implementations; one-bar delay test; hold-time distributions; net Sharpe with block bootstrap; within-run shuffle surrogate.
findings: Net-positive out of sample with a Sharpe interval clear of zero: 0 of 76 definition x timeframe scores (cell 17).
Best case ema_cross_50_200 at 4h: breakeven 5.611 bp vs 0.5395 bp to cross, net +540 bp, Sharpe 0.33 [-0.17, 0.82] on 107 trades, surrogate -0.20.
At 1h and below every candidate is net-negative with intervals containing zero. Median hold spans two orders of magnitude and break-even tracks it.
Warning case: mtf_coarse_only_1h_4h at 30m has Sharpe 1.26 on shuffled bars vs -0.22 on real bars.
One-bar delay lowers gross for causal rules (e.g. swing_5 gross 207.5 bp vs -123.9 delayed); all 18 causality assertions pass.
lookahead_detail: trend.pivots uses rolling_max(center=True) at trend.py:218-219 but a pivot is confirmed at bar j+k and the position changes only then (trend.py:224); assertions 'never acts at the bar the pivot occurred' pass and delay test loses gross.
validity_issues: Cost is a fixed 0.6 pip (0.5395 bp), about a third of the measured 1.6 pips median in notebook 19.
Only 107 trades in the best cell, single instrument.
Shuffled surrogate exposes autocorrelation artefacts (mtf rule scores 1.26 on shuffled data).
edge_summary: No definition pays: 0 of 76 net-positive with a Sharpe CI excluding zero; best ema_cross_50_200 4h net +540 bp but Sharpe 0.33 with CI [-0.17, 0.82].
recommendation: Avoid classical trend rules as standalone alpha. Reuse the causality assertion pattern and the shuffled-bar surrogate control; if trend is used as a feature, use long-horizon rules where hold time (not signal) provides the breakeven margin.

topic: Measured feature windows and shadow-feature selection for volatility forecasting
purpose: Replace inherited constants (lags 1/5/22/66, normaliser 240) with windows measured from integrated autocorrelation time, widen to 511 candidate columns, and keep only columns beating block-permuted shadow copies.
data_sources: EURUSD at 15m/30m/1h/4h, 6 folds each, development only; 511 distinct candidates vs 12 fixed; target next-bar log range.
methods: Integrated autocorrelation time (Sokal windowing) on deseasonalised log range; paired block bootstrap of correlation delta vs baseline and HAR-RV; block-permutation shadow columns for selection.
findings: Inherited 240-bar normaliser is 0.23x the measured span at 15m (1056 bars = 11 days), 0.42x at 30m (576), 0.77x at 1h (312) and 2.86x at 4h (84).
Gain over baseline is +0.0131 to +0.0176 CI at 15m, +0.0102 to +0.0143 at 30m, and zero at 1h; per-fold delta 15m mean +0.0154, 1h +0.0002.
Columns kept on all 6 folds: 25 of 719 timeframe-column pairs; top are season sin_h1 (4h importance 0.506) and volume volz windows.
Importance distribution of 4,314 candidates: median 0.0000, skew 24.9, kurtosis 654.7, max 0.610.
lookahead_detail: Windows estimated on the training slice per fold; selection null uses block-permuted shadows. Sealed tail not read.
validity_issues: Predicts volatility only, largely seasonality plus volume.
Final 'What it says' cell defers to CLAUDE.md rather than stating numeric conclusions.
EURUSD only, 4 timeframes.
edge_summary: Measured windows add +0.012 to +0.016 correlation at 15m/30m (CI excludes zero) and nothing at 1h; no direction or trading claim.
recommendation: Reuse the idea that normalisation windows must be measured per timeframe (integrated autocorrelation) and the shadow-feature selection null. Expect little gain from wider feature sets.

topic: Scale-free TA-Lib indicator matrices for 18 pairs x 7 timeframes
purpose: Reports the pipeline that computes 160 TA-Lib functions (179 outputs) per pair/timeframe, transforms each output to a scale-free form, audits and drops failures; infrastructure only.
data_sources: 18 pairs x 7 timeframes = 126 matrices, 51,003,432 rows, 20.0 GB, 15 minutes compute, written to data/forex/<PAIR>/talib_<tf>.parquet (the data/forex cache no longer exists on disk).
methods: Per-output transform chosen on the training slice (pct100, log_ratio, ratio, bars_ago, causal z at measured window, none); norm audit; pattern firing rates.
findings: Transform mix over 22,528 columns: pct100 49.0%, log_ratio 25.2%, zscore 16.0%, none 5.8%, bars_ago 2.2%, ratio 1.7%.
Dropped after audit: AD (15 matrices, drifts 1.28 sd), ACOS/ASIN (track price level), OBV (1 matrix); MAVP skipped (needs periods input).
Candlestick pattern firing rate over 61 patterns x timeframes on EURUSD: mean 5.55%, median 0.39%, max 99.3%; 18 patterns never fire at some timeframes (e.g. CDL3STARSINSOUTH, CDLMATHOLD).
lookahead_detail: Transforms measured on the training slice; z-score windows causal. Warmup rows null. Not audited against forward targets.
validity_issues: No predictive test of any indicator; 179 outputs would inflate multiple testing.
Talib parquet files referenced in the notebook are not on disk any more (data/forex retired), so cells reading them cannot rerun.
edge_summary: None: feature-engineering infrastructure, no relation to returns tested.
recommendation: Reuse the measured-transform-per-output approach and the norm audit when building MNQ technical features; do not treat TA-Lib outputs as evidence of edge, and prune with a selection null.

topic: Continuous multi-scale Parkinson variance ladder and rho (trending vs oscillating) feature
purpose: Build windows ending at every minute for a ladder (5,15,30,60,240,1440,4320 minutes), test the rho efficiency statistic against an order-destroyed null, and compare the block to clock-grid features for forecasting the next window's range and rho.
data_sources: EURUSD 1m 2.2M bars, contiguous vs activity bases; results/73-75 (336 score rows, 1,260 selection rows); horizons 15/60/240 minutes; targets y_next_lr and y_next_rho.
methods: Rolling OHLC windows, Parkinson integrated variance, rho = ln(iv_agg/iv_sum), within-run block-shuffle null, paired block bootstrap vs clock13 and HAR-RV, phase-offset test, shadow-column selection.
findings: Longest gap-free run is 1,440 bars, so windows of 1 day or more have 0-1 valid rows on the contiguous basis; only the activity basis reaches the top of the ladder.
rho mean is -0.0008 (5 min) to -0.054 (1440 min); real-vs-null z about -250 to -359 on the contiguous basis (Jensen offset plus order effects).
Phase spread: clock-grid phase 0 vs other offsets differs by 0.0017 (15m), 0.0079 (60m), 0.0090 (240m) in correlation.
y_next_rho (direction-agnostic trendiness) is barely predictable: correlation 0.084 (15m), 0.053 (60m), 0.035 (240m).
lookahead_detail: Windows end at each minute and use only past bars; targets shift(-horizon) (multiscale.py:306-307) standardised by trailing stats. Rows overlap heavily (adjacent minute windows share most bars), so bootstrap uses one-week blocks.
validity_issues: Section 8 'What this establishes' is a template that defers to the tables.
Highly overlapping minute rows; phase experiment shows the clock grid is not special, but block bootstrap intervals still rely on autocorrelation assumptions.
Volatility target only.
edge_summary: Multi-scale variance ladder adds +0.0256 correlation at a 15-minute horizon and +0.010 at 60 minutes (CIs exclude zero) but 0 at 240 minutes; trendiness (rho) next window is essentially unpredictable (corr 0.03-0.09). No return edge.
recommendation: Include the Parkinson variance-per-unit-time ladder and rolling-window construction for the MNQ volatility modality (short horizons benefit most). Use activity-basis windows across session breaks and add explicit elapsed-clock columns. Do not expect it to forecast trend/efficiency.

topic: Stylised facts of EURUSD returns against geometric Brownian motion
purpose: Test Gaussianity, constant volatility, independence, continuity and variance scaling; quantify how often tail events arrive versus Gaussian expectation.
data_sources: EURUSD 1m to 1d, within-run returns (2,188,970 at 1m, 1,876 at 1d); results/76-78 (7 assumption rows, 70 tail rows, 49 variance-ratio rows).
methods: Distribution statistics, |r| autocorrelation, Lo-MacKinlay heteroskedasticity-robust variance ratios, Parkinson/close ratio, variance-scaling slope, exceedance counts vs Gaussian (unconditional and causal-standardised).
findings: |r| autocorrelation at lag 1: 0.325 (1m), 0.309 (5m), 0.291 (15m), 0.256 (1h), 0.165 (4h), 0.126 (1d): strong volatility clustering.
Variance ratios stay near 1 (e.g. VR(2)=0.998 at 1m, 0.980 at 5m, 0.987 at 1h, 1.017 at 4h); implied Hurst 0.479, variance scaling slope 0.958.
Parkinson/close sigma ratio 0.898 at 1m, 0.955 at 5m, 0.983 at 15m, 1.002 at 1h, 1.011 at 1d.
4-sigma events occur about 100x more often than Gaussian at 1m (ratio 102.5 unconditional, 97.7 causal) and 5-sigma about 5,595x (4,438 causal).
Largest hourly move is +17.4 sigma (+1.744%) on 2022-11-10 13:00 UTC; the top 15 land mostly on macro-release hours.
lookahead_detail: Descriptive statistics; the causal-standardised tail rows divide by a trailing sigma ending at t-1.
validity_issues: 'What this establishes' is a template referring to tables; no OOS test needed for descriptive stats.
EURUSD only.
edge_summary: None: confirms independence (variance ratios near 1, Hurst 0.479) so direction is close to a random walk, and that volatility clusters strongly.
recommendation: Use the stylised facts to justify volatility-normalised targets/stops and heavy-tail-aware losses; assume MNQ is similarly near-martingale in direction and plan for a fat left tail in risk. Re-run on MNQ before relying on the numbers.

topic: Nearest-neighbour vector store of 35-dim market states for range forecasting
purpose: Store sealed per-fold corpora of multiscale state vectors in DuckDB vss, test whether analog retrieval forecasts the next hour's log range, and analyse the space (PCA, t-SNE, kNN graph, communities, density-as-confidence).
data_sources: EURUSD 1h states from data/vectors/eurusd.duckdb: 6 sealed corpora f1-f6 (4,157 to 24,566 rows), 86,495 stored rows = 24,566 distinct states 2020-01-21 13:00 to 2024-02-23 15:00; 63 scored rows; 22,616 validation rows pooled.
methods: Walk-forward sealed corpora (usable_from = ts_max + horizon), kNN averaging with k in {1,5,20,50,100,400}, paired block bootstrap vs gbr/har_ms/persistence, relative contrast vs Gaussian, Leiden communities vs Gaussian surrogate.
findings: Correlation with next-hour log range: gbr 0.7008, knn_k100 0.6873 (0.0135 below gbr, +0.0417 above har_ms), knn_k50 0.6859, har_ms 0.6457, persistence 0.6424, knn_k1 0.4620 (R2 -0.07); kNN wins all 6 folds vs har_ms, loses all 6 vs gbr.
Relative contrast 10.09 on real states vs 1.22 for a Gaussian surrogate; effective dimension 8.25 of 35 (90% variance in 14 components).
Leiden: 14 communities, modularity 0.7545 vs 0.3261 surrogate; they are volatility x hour-of-day (quiet Asian hours vs London/NY overlap), not years.
Distance to analogs does not predict forecast error: correlation +0.004 across 3,735 queries; correlation by density decile rises 0.59 to 0.84 only because target sd rises.
HNSW WHERE-filter silently returns a short result set (5 vs 1 neighbours) so cutoffs must be applied at corpus-write time.
lookahead_detail: Corpus sealed per fold with derived usable_from and search() refuses earlier query stamps; stride equals horizon to avoid overlap; standardiser fitted on the corpus. The live example query 2025-07-16 15:46 is beyond every corpus end (2024-02-23).
validity_issues: Target is volatility; retrieval mostly recovers a volatility x session gradient (PC1) rather than nonlinear structure.
kNN loses to gradient boosting on all folds; no direction forecast is tested here.
Corpus ends 2024-02-23 while data run to 2026-01-05; sealed tail unscored.
edge_summary: kNN analogs beat HAR by +0.042 correlation on the next-hour range (CI [0.037, 0.047]) but trail gradient boosting by 0.0135; the retrieved neighbours carry volatility and time-of-day, not direction. No trading edge measured.
recommendation: Consider a sealed, time-gated analog-retrieval modality as a regime/volatility conditioner for the MNQ model, with the same write-time cutoff discipline. Use k of 50-400 and average outcomes; do not use distance as a confidence signal.

topic: Read-only browser of the EURUSD DuckDB vector store
purpose: Show the store's tables, schema, sample rows, a search with round-trip check and raw SQL; no analysis.
data_sources: data/vectors/eurusd.duckdb (39.9 MB): tables corpora + states_f1_h60..f6_h60, FLOAT[35] vectors, y_next_lr; f6 has 24,566 states. The saved output prints an old path e:\source\repos\Trading\forexmodel\data\vectors.

Example probe search returns 8 analogs at distance 11.3-11.9 with analog forecast 1.122 (spread 0.515).
