topic: EMA(9)/SMA(21) and triple-EMA crossings on MNQ 5-minute bars: event study, indicator separation, expectancy vs holding period
purpose: Ask what happens after an EMA9/SMA21 crossing, whether indicators known at the crossing predict a 2-bar follow-through, and whether expectancy after cost turns positive at longer holds.
data_sources: Lake table bars (Iceberg market.bars, real UTC) symbol MNQZ5 timeframe 1m via lean/scripts/lake_bars.py, clipped to 09:30-17:00 New York and consolidated per session to 5m. Window 2025-09-29 to 2025-12-18 (59 sessions; my read-only SQL gives 5,217 RTH 5m bars). Companion file research/crossing_events.csv (386 rows, 23 columns).
methods: Crossing detection on sign(EMA9-SMA21) and a triple-EMA stack; label 'held 2 bars' (next two closes AND opens move with the trade); aligned event-study paths; Welch t-tests and Cohen d for 11 indicators at the crossing (RSI14, MACD, ATR14, realized vol 20, bar range/ATR, EMA-SMA gap, volume/20-bar mean, minute of day); hit rate by indicator quintile; net expectancy vs holding horizon 1..24 bars with 95% bands; cost 1.78 fee + 1.0211 slippage = $2.8011 round trip = 0.554 bp.
findings: The notebook has no saved outputs. I re-ran its own function definitions read-only on the same lake query; the result reproduces the saved crossing_events.csv exactly: 249 EMA9/SMA21 crossings and 137 triple-EMA crossings (csv value_counts), 59 sessions.

EMA9/SMA21: 22.1% (55 of 249) held two bars. Mean signed 2-bar forward return +2.175 bp, SE 0.955, t 2.28, sd 15.07. Cost is 0.554 bp, so net +1.62 bp per crossing (about +$8 per contract per trade). Long crossings (123) average -0.96 bp, short crossings (126) +5.23 bp: the whole gross mean is the short side in a Q4 2025 sample that ended near where it began (24,852 to 24,986).

Horizon sweep (my replication of cell 22): EMA9/SMA21 net of cost is positive at 24 of 24 horizons (best 21 bars, +2.64 bp, 95% half-width 5.41 bp; horizon 2: +1.62 +/- 1.88, i.e. the interval covers zero). Triple-EMA net is positive at only 6 of 24 horizons and negative for most horizons above 6 bars (-1.2 to -2.1 bp at 8-12 bars).

The notebook's hard-coded headlines contradict its own numbers: 'the average path never clears cost', 'no quintile of any indicator reaches break-even' (computed break-even hit rate 14.3%, base rate 22.1%, quintile hit rates run 12% to 36%) and 'the 2-bar rule never turns positive' (net is positive at 2 bars). These strings predate the switch to lake bars and were not updated.

Indicators at the crossing barely separate held from not-held: Welch p = bar_range_ticks 0.008, ATR14 0.012, RSI14 0.043, realized_vol_20 0.046, bar_range/ATR 0.080, EMA-SMA gap 0.204, MACD hist 0.951. None survives Bonferroni over 11 tests (0.0045). The only monotone pattern is volatility: hit rate 16% in the lowest ATR% quintile rising to 34% in the top; bar_range/ATR 12% to 36% at the fourth quintile. This is the same magnitude effect the magnitude notebook measures.
Cost model: $2.80 round trip on MNQ equals 1.40 points, identical to the quantlab OOS cost (1.40055 points).
lookahead_detail: Indicator features (EMA seeded at x[0], SMA rolling min_periods=21, Wilder RSI/ATR, MACD) are trailing and computed on the crossing bar's close. 'achieved_two_bar_hold' and forward_return_2_bar use bars i+1..i+2 and are labels only; the notebook itself flags that comparing held vs missed after bar 0 is label-circular (section 10). Entry is priced at the crossing bar's close (optimistic fill, no next-bar-open), and EMA/SMA state runs across session boundaries by design (cell 8, crossing_bars only skips cross detection across sessions).
edge_summary: EMA9/SMA21 crossings show a gross 2-bar signed return of +2.18 bp (t 2.28, n=249) and +1.62 bp net of a 0.554 bp cost, but it comes entirely from shorts (+5.23 bp vs -0.96 bp long) in one 59-session, single-contract window, the net interval covers zero at every horizon, and crossings cluster so the effective n is smaller than 249. No indicator at the crossing separates good from bad crossings after multiplicity, other than bar size relative to ATR. Not an edge; an in-sample curiosity.
validity_issues: Stale hard-coded conclusions (titles and print statements) that the replicated numbers contradict.
Single contract MNQZ5, one quarter (59 sessions), 249 crossings, clustered events so bands are too narrow (notebook section 10 says so).
Break-even hit rate 14.3% is defined on the future-dependent 'held' label, so comparing quintile hit rates to it is not a tradable test.
Fill at crossing close; no next-bar fill or latency; slippage is a quoted-spread lower bound.
11 t-tests and 6 quintile panels with no multiplicity correction; no train/test split anywhere.
reusable_assets: Event-study and horizon-sweep pattern (cells 14 and 22) in crossing_analysis.ipynb
Indicator set with full-word names in FEATURES (cell 6): RSI14, MACD, ATR14, realized_volatility_20_basis_points, bar_range_over_average_true_range, volume_over_20_bar_mean
E:/source/repos/ml_dashboard/Trading/quant/lean/Casual Red Flamingo/research/crossing_events.csv (386 labelled events, timestamps New York tz-aware)
recommendation: Do not build a crossing rule into the multimodal model. Reuse (a) the cost figure 0.554 bp / 1.40 points round trip, (b) the finding that the size of the current bar relative to ATR is the one thing that separates follow-through from none, which feeds a volatility/magnitude input, and (c) the event-study plus horizon-sweep template with a label-circularity guard. Re-derive any crossing statistic on a train-only window and never quote the hard-coded titles.

topic: Forecasting the magnitude (next-hour realized variance) versus direction of MNQ 5-minute moves
purpose: Show with a purged rolling walk-forward, HAC standard errors, Giacomini-White/Clark-West tests, block bootstrap and permutation nulls that volatility is forecastable while direction is not.
data_sources: Lake table bars, symbol MNQZ5, 1m to 5m, RTH 09:30-17:00 New York, 2025-09-29 to 2025-12-18, 59 sessions, 4,565 usable rows after windowing (my SQL).
methods: Target: log of mean squared 5m return over the next 12 bars (never crossing a session). Predictors: log trailing realized variance at 12, 84 and 252 valid bars (HAR) plus a per-intraday-slot clock factor fitted on training rows only. Rolling fixed-length origin 1,200 train / 11 purge / 120 test = 27 folds. Baseline: train mean. Nested-model tests (GW, CW, Holm), QLIKE, VIF and circular block bootstrap, global and within-slot permutation nulls, sign-flip no-op, deliberate centred-window leak as positive control. Direction: same scheme on mean forward return with previous return, 12-bar ROC and log variance.
findings: The notebook has no saved outputs, so I ran its own function definitions (cells 9, 13, 17, 21, 25) read-only against my own SQL pull of the same bars. The headline reproduces: HAR+clock out-of-sample R2 +0.5226 (notebook +0.523), correlation +0.6938 (notebook +0.694), 3,240 test rows, 27 folds all positive (worst fold +0.074, median +0.506).

Model ladder pooled OOS R2 (log-variance scale, my run): constant 0.000, clock only +0.076, variance 1 hour +0.480, HAR (1h,1d,3d) +0.483, HAR+clock +0.523. Almost all skill is the persistence of the last hour's variance; the clock adds about +0.04.
Direction, same scheme: R2 -0.0215 (notebook -0.022), correlation -0.079, sign accuracy 0.4693 on an effective n of about 362 (my run).
Leak guard works: fitting the clock factor on the full sample gives R2 +0.5336 vs +0.5226 honest, so the leak is worth +0.011.

The notebook's own caveat (cell 10): 3,240 test rows at horizon 12 is at most about 270 non-overlapping hours, so 'HAR+clock beats HAR' is probably not separable. Tables for Ljung-Box, HAC, GW/CW, VIF and permutation p-values exist only as code; I did not run the 200-draw permutation loops.

A variance forecast is not a P&L: MNQ has no tradable volatility instrument here; the notebook states the use is sizing, stop distance and gating bars whose expected move cannot clear the 0.554 bp round trip.
lookahead_detail: Well guarded. trailing_realized_variance uses only valid past returns with min_periods=window; forward_realized_variance is the target only; clock_factor is re-estimated per fold on rows [0, upto) of the training slice (cell 17, upto = last train bar + 1); purge of 11 rows matches the 12-bar label overlap; the centred_realized_variance arm is a deliberate positive control. One residual: the R2 baseline is the train mean of log variance, which is generous to a persistent series.
edge_summary: Predictive edge in volatility: HAR+clock explains +0.52 of out-of-sample log-variance (corr 0.69, all 27 rolling folds positive), replicated by me from the lake. topic: Is there a statistically measurable trend in MNQ 5-minute closes; standardized rate of change as a trend statistic
purpose: Compare four trend detectors, propose the standardized ROC t_k = ln(P_t/P_{t-k}) / (sigma_hat*sqrt(k)), and test the forward value of its signals against a sign-shuffled null after cost.
data_sources: Lake bars symbol MNQZ5 1m to 5m, RTH 09:30-17:00 NY, 2025-09-29 to 2025-12-18, 5,158 within-session returns, 59 sessions (my SQL pull).
methods: Descriptive eight-number distribution; Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio with heteroskedasticity-robust z*; t_k for lookbacks 6/12/24 and thresholds 0.5-2.0; mean signed cumulative forward return over 30 bars per (k, theta) cell with MAE/MFE; sign-shuffled null for the peak (max over 30 horizons); autocorrelation of t_k vs lag in units of k.
findings: No saved outputs. I re-ran cells 8, 10, 12, 14 and 15 read-only (150 null draws instead of 300). 5-minute log return: mean -0.070 bp, median +0.097, sd 9.634, skew -0.377, excess kurtosis 6.32, p25 -3.96, p75 +4.16, min -86.77, max +63.30; exact zeros 0.89%.

Variance ratio: VR 1.031 (10 min) rising to 1.224 (180 min), 1.211 (240 min). Homoskedastic z is 1.9 to 2.5 (would read as significant) but the robust z* is 1.25 to 1.69, below 1.96 at every horizon, matching the notebook's '|z*| <= 1.70'.

Forward paths (mean signed cumulative return): best cell k=12, theta=1.5, 582 signals, peak +6.33 bp at bar 11 (net of 0.554 bp cost +5.78), MAE -39.9 bp, MFE +40.2 bp; k=6, theta=1.5: +5.11 bp at bar 12, n=560; k=24 cells peak below +0.9 bp.

Null-of-the-maximum (sign-shuffled, same freedom to pick the best of 30 horizons): mean 3.34 bp, sd 4.17, p95 12.99; the measured peak gives z = 0.72, p = 0.17 (notebook: 300 draws). So the +6 bp is not distinguishable from selection noise.
Autocorrelation of t_k at lag = k: -0.0002 (k=6), +0.012 (k=12), -0.035 (k=24), against lag-1 of 0.83 to 0.96: the state's memory is only the overlap of its own window.
Verdict in the notebook (no trend to find on these bars) is supported by my replication.
lookahead_detail: t_k uses a trailing 120-bar sigma with min_periods=window and price at t and t-k only; forward_paths measures the future only as an outcome and truncates at session end. State runs continuously across the overnight gap (the 120-bar volatility window spans sessions), which is causal but mixes overnight variance into sigma.
edge_summary: No trading edge: 1.5-sigma standardized ROC signals show +5 to +6 bp gross drift over 5-12 bars in-sample (n=560-582, overlapping) but that peak is within the sign-shuffled null of the maximum (p 0.17), and the variance ratios are indistinguishable from a random walk under the robust test.
validity_issues: Whole 59-session window in-sample; no split (notebook item 1).
Nine (k, theta) cells and 30 horizons searched with only the horizon maximum corrected in the null; overlapping windows so effective n is about signals/k.
Single expiry, one regime (flat drift, -0.07 bp mean).
Q4 2025 lies inside the project's locked holdout window.
reusable_assets: standardized_rate_of_change(prices, lookback, volatility_window=120) in trend_detection.ipynb cell 12: a scale-free, causal momentum feature
variance_ratio (Lo-MacKinlay with robust z*) and sign_shuffled null generator
recommendation: Include t_k at k in {6,12,24} as low-cost causal inputs and use the same sign-shuffled null-of-the-maximum test to decide whether any learned momentum feature earns its place; do not expect a trend feature alone to carry a win rate. Repeat on multi-year data before drawing any conclusion, since 59 sessions cannot resolve a 5 bp effect.

topic: Descriptive statistics of MNQ candle body size and range, by time of day
purpose: Characterize the distribution of |close-open| relative to the global mean, run lengths of above-average bars, and 'mechanical vs discretionary' sessions by time of day, on 96.7M bars, 2019-2025.
data_sources: QuestDB HTTP /exp, table ohlcv, symbol 'MNQ', 2019-05-05 15:03 to 2025-12-30 15:59 (96,735,629 rows; 2025 alone 16.9M rows). QuestDB was retired on 2026-09-10; the rows are 1-SECOND bars although the notebook calls them 1-minute. Executed May 2026 (file mtime May 4).
methods: body_ratio = |c-o| / global mean; z-scores and percentile ranks over the whole 7-year series; run-length encoding of body_ratio > 1; Eastern-time 30-minute buckets and session labels; rolling 20/50/100 body ratio; 5m and 15m resamples.
findings: Saved outputs: mean |body| 0.4337 pts, mean range 0.7200 pts; body-ratio quantiles p50 0.576x, p75 1.153x, p90 2.306x, p99 7.49x, p99.9 14.99x; p10 and p25 are exactly 0 (over a quarter of bars have zero body). Sigma thresholds +1 sd 2.624x (9.59% of bars), +3 sd 5.873x (1.62%).
Above-average runs: 17,413,657 runs, mean length 2.0 bars, median 1, max 302, p95 6; 28.4% of above-average bars are isolated singles, 7.7% are in runs over 10.

Time-of-day table: stamped 02:30 'ET' is the busiest bucket (avg body 2.232x, avg volume 3.32x, 14.1% of bars above 2 sd), and 09:30 'open' is quiet (0.595x body, 0.33x volume). Session labels put 55,971,944 of 96.7M bars in 'overnight'.

Correlation(body_ratio, volume_ratio) = 0.5636; 91.4% of >2 sd body bars also have above-average volume. Rolling body ratio > 1.0x about 35.6-35.8% of the time; 801,526 rising crossings of 1.5x at the 20-bar mean.
5m resample (469,851 bars) and 15m (156,663 bars): p50 0.563x/0.565x, p90 2.359x/2.341x, above-average runs mean 2.0: the normalized distribution is scale-invariant across timeframes by construction.

The 'ET' buckets are mislabelled: the snapshot stores Pacific wall time in a UTC column. Independent check by me: ohlcv_1m MNQ Jan-May 2025 mean volume peaks at stamped 06:30 (6,595), the true 09:30 ET cash open, so converting to US/Eastern shifts every bucket 3 hours early and puts the real RTH open into 'overnight'/'pre_market' and the 'MECH/DISC' conclusions are inverted for the cash session.
lookahead_detail: Descriptive study with no model, but body_ratio, body_z and body_pctrank use whole-series (2019-2025) mean, sd and rank (cell 4), which would leak future information if reused as features; the rolling 20/50/100 means (cell 18) are trailing and causal. Time-of-day analysis uses wrong-clock timestamps.
edge_summary: No trading or predictive claim is made or tested. The only quantitative relationship is body size vs volume (r 0.56), a same-bar association, not a forecast.
validity_issues: Timestamps are Pacific wall time labelled UTC, then converted to US/Eastern: all time-of-day and session results are shifted.
Bars are 1-second sparse bars, described as 1-minute; 25% zero-body bars dominate the lower quantiles and the run-length statistics.
Whole-series normalization; pooled 2019-2025 with regime and volume changes; bare root symbol 'MNQ' (raw prices spliced at rolls).

topic: Walk-forward out-of-sample results of a 1-minute OHLCV-geometry transformer on MNQ, 2023-2025
purpose: Read back fold-level results (recipe quant_oos_v1) and show whether a next-bar return forecast beats predicting zero and whether conviction gating can beat costs; includes a break-even directional-accuracy calculator.
data_sources: Marimo notebook reading s3://derived/recipe=quant_oos_v1/table=folds and table=conviction. That prefix is NOT present in the lake today (my query returned 'No files found', and no derived_ view exists), so cell 2 errors as written. The same output is on disk: Trading/quantlab/results/folds.parquet, conviction.parquet, summary.json. Underlying run: MNQ 1m, 1,059,776 bars, 2023-01-02 to 2025-12-30, 1,048,713 windows.
methods: Six expanding-window folds (train through fold k, purge 512 windows, test the next equal slice, 898,385 test windows total); transformer with model width 64, sequence 32, 6 scale-free candle features with trailing 256-bar z-score; target next-bar log return scaled by train std; scoring vs predict-zero; cost 1.40055 points ($2.80) round trip converted at the traded price; conviction gating at the top 100/25/10/5/1% by |prediction|.
findings: Pooled OOS R2 vs predict-zero -0.000954; all 6 folds negative (-0.0019, -0.0018, -0.0004, -0.0023, -0.0003, -0.0008); fold-mean R2 -0.00124 with bootstrap CI [-0.00185, -0.00063]. Source: results/summary.json pooled block.

Pooled directional accuracy 0.50658 (folds 0.4987, 0.5111, 0.5124, 0.5058, 0.5048, 0.5067; CI [0.5030, 0.5098]); Spearman IC +0.0093. Statistically distinguishable from 0.5 on 898k windows, economically tiny.
Persistence baseline is worse than zero: persistence R2 about -1.0 in every fold (copy-last-return MSE 2.23e-7 vs zero 1.11e-7), so zero is the bar.

Cost: gross mean return per trade +8.8e-7 log return vs net -7.2e-5 (cost about 82 times the gross edge at full trading; conviction gating at the top 10% gives accuracy 0.5174, gross +2.5e-6, net -7.0e-5, still about 28 times). The notebook's prose says 'roughly forty times'.

Break-even calculator (cell 9, defaults): cost 1.40055 pts / 19,808 = 7.07e-5, E|y| 1.8344e-4 -> break-even directional accuracy 0.6927 vs measured 0.5066: shortfall 18.6 percentage points, edge needed 29 times edge held.
Target distribution (summary.json): sd 3.37e-4, skew -1.69, kurtosis 543.7, min -0.0460, max +0.0247; extremes indicate unfiltered gaps or contract-roll steps in the 1m volume-roll series.

Related HPO on volume bars (results/hpo_summary.json): return R2 -0.0015 and direction 0.5021 on the holdout, but volatility R2 +0.553 vs 0.466 for a linear last-realized-vol baseline, consistent with the magnitude notebook.
lookahead_detail: Features are trailing z-scores with min_periods=256 (data.py normalize); window i ends at row i+31 and the target is the log return of the next bar (data.py window_into_tensor); target scale uses train std only (evaluate.py); purge 512 windows exceeds sequence 32 + normalization 256. Caveats: entry is assumed at the window-end close (no latency or next-bar-open fill), and data.load_bars imports lake_bars from a path that does not exist (see transformer_pipeline), so it cannot be re-run unchanged. Fold 5's test (2025-07-29 to 2025-12-30) sits inside the locked holdout, and the same period was used in prior notebooks.
edge_summary: No edge in a pure 1-minute candle-geometry transformer: negative R2 in 6 of 6 folds, directional accuracy 0.5066 against a cost break-even of 0.693, net -7.2e-5 log return per trade (about -1.4 points), and no conviction threshold rescues it. Only the magnitude of the prediction carries a trace of information.
validity_issues: Results table not landed in the lake, so the marimo notebook fails; numbers exist only in quantlab/results.
Volume-roll continuous series is not back-adjusted and gaps/weekends are not excluded from targets.
Six folds only; 1-minute predictions overlap in information; fold 0 at 0.4987 vs others above 0.5.

Notebook default credentials in the cell are the local-dev lake keys (not a modelling issue).

recommendation: Treat as the honest null for candle-only models: a next-bar return head on 1m OHLCV geometry has no edge and cannot be a signal source for the multimodal model. Reuse the evaluation harness, the break-even accuracy formula and the 1.40-point cost, and use these fold results as the baseline any new modality must beat. Move to longer horizons and a target that is not next-bar sign; avoid next-bar direction as the objective.
